title: The Year of the Elephant
hook: An army with an elephant marched on the Ka'bah. It never arrived. That same year, a boy named Muhammad was born.

screens.text: **An army marched on the Ka'bah, with an elephant at the front.** It never arrived. That same year, in the same town, a baby boy was born.

**The army of the elephant.** A powerful army came to destroy the Ka'bah, bringing an elephant. It was turned back. The Qur'an says Allah sent against them *"birds in flocks"* [Q 105:3, Saheeh Intl.].
bubbles: A whole **surah** (chapter) tells it in five short verses: Surah al-Fil, "The Elephant" [Q 105:1–5].
The Arabs remembered it so well that they called that year the Year of the Elephant [IslamQA 147601].

screens.text: **A baby in Makkah.** That same year, about 570 CE, Muhammad ﷺ was born in Makkah, on a Monday [Muslim 1162; IslamQA 147601]. The month was Rabi' al-Awwal, by most accounts.
bubbles: Years later he fasted on Mondays. Asked why, he said it was the day he was born [Muslim 1162].
His father, 'Abdullah, had died before he was born [IslamQA 11575; Dar al-Ifta 168].

events.title: The hijra
events.text: After thirteen years of preaching in Makkah, he moves to Madinah [Bukhari 3902].

events.title: His death
events.text: He dies in Madinah, ten years after the move [Bukhari 3902; Yaqeen].

screens.text: **A family line back to Isma'il.** His clan was Banu Hashim, part of Quraysh, the tribe that ran Makkah. Their line went back to Isma'il, the son who helped raise the Ka'bah [Muslim 2276; IslamQA 289868].
bubbles: The early biographers say his grandfather, 'Abd al-Muttalib, chose his name: Muhammad, which means "the much-praised" [Qalam ep. 9; Dar al-Ifta 167].

screens.prompt: Put his family line in order, from the widest to the closest [Muslim 2276].
screens.feedback: He described his own line this way: chosen from Isma'il's descendants, down through Kinanah, Quraysh and Banu Hashim [Muslim 2276].

screens.text: **Protected, with no father there.** He never met his father. The same Lord who turned back an army was caring for a baby who had already lost so much. Allah's plan never depended on who was standing beside him.
bubbles: If you're building a life of faith without the family support you hoped for, his story starts in that same place. Your worth was never about who stands behind you.

options.feedback: Yes. Allah protected His House, and a baby whose father was gone. Then let people help too.

options.text: Feeling this alone means I made a mistake
options.feedback: Not quite. Loneliness is a feeling, not a verdict. The Prophet ﷺ himself began life with a loss.

options.text: Keep it all inside until things get better on their own
options.feedback: Not quite. Hard seasons are easier shared. Talk to {{mentor.name}}, or ask the AI guide for ideas.

check.prompt: What happened in the Year of the Elephant?

options.text: An army came to destroy the Ka'bah and Allah turned it back; the Prophet ﷺ was born that year
options.feedback: Right. Surah al-Fil tells the story [Q 105:1–5], and he was born in Makkah that same year.

options.text: The Ka'bah was destroyed and rebuilt
options.feedback: Not quite. The army never reached it. Allah turned it back with birds in flocks [Q 105:1–5].

check.prompt: Who was the Prophet's ﷺ father, and what happened to him?

options.text: 'Abdullah, who died before his son was born
options.feedback: Right. He was born already without a father, and still protected.

options.text: 'Abd al-Muttalib, who raised him from birth
options.feedback: Not quite. 'Abd al-Muttalib was his grandfather. His father 'Abdullah died before he was born.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- An army "of the elephant" came to destroy the Ka'bah; Allah turned it back with birds in flocks [Q 105:1–5].
- The Prophet ﷺ was born in Makkah in the Year of the Elephant, about 570 CE (some calculate 571) [IslamQA 147601; Yaqeen; Qalam ep. 9]; on a Monday [Muslim 1162]; in Rabi' al-Awwal by most accounts. The exact day is disputed (2nd, 8th, 9th, 10th, 12th or 17th are all reported; IslamQA 147601 calls 8th–12th the strongest range). (scholar question Q44)
- Lineage: Muhammad son of 'Abdullah son of 'Abd al-Muttalib, of Banu Hashim of Quraysh, from the descendants of Isma'il [Muslim 2276; IslamQA 289868].
- His father 'Abdullah died before he was born [IslamQA 11575; Qalam ep. 8; Dar al-Ifta Egypt, seerah part 2].
- The early biographers say 'Abd al-Muttalib named him; "Muhammad" means the much-praised [Qalam ep. 9; Dar al-Ifta Egypt, seerah part 1 for the meaning]. Keep the naming as "the early biographers say".
- Life outline used in the timeline: revelation at forty, thirteen years in Makkah, ten in Madinah, died at sixty-three [Bukhari 3902]; 622 CE and 632 CE [Yaqeen; Dar al-Ifta Egypt].

**Likely questions**
- *"When exactly is his birthday?"* Rabi' al-Awwal by most accounts; the day is disputed, and scholars give several dates. Don't pick one. (scholar question Q44)
- *"Should I celebrate the Mawlid?"* Scholars differ on celebrating his birthday. Don't argue either side; offer "Ask my imam" so the convert hears their masjid's view.
- *"Did amazing things happen when he was born?"* Some well-known stories (a Persian palace shaking, a sacred fire going out) have chains scholars question, so this track leaves them out. (scholar question Q43)
- *"Who led the army?"* The Qur'an doesn't name him. Say the Qur'an's account is what's certain and that the early biographers give more detail; offer to go deeper only with sources from this lesson.
- *"My family won't talk to me."* Respond with care: listen first, then offer practical steps (keep kind contact open, lean on the mentor, Day 35's skills for family). If there's any danger (being thrown out, violence), follow the safety rule.

**Escalate:** celebrating the Mawlid (Q44); any family conflict that is unsafe (safety rule, never only the imam queue).

**Don't**
- Don't give a single birth date as fact.
- Don't tell the birth-wonder stories as fact; if asked, they are "well-known stories whose chains scholars consider weak".
- Don't argue for or against Mawlid celebrations.
- Don't describe the Prophet's ﷺ appearance as a baby or picture him.
